original_question: Let chi_{8d} denote the quadratic character attached to the fundamental discriminant 8d, with d ranging over odd squarefree integers 0 < d < X. Determine a polynomial P of degree 10 such that sum L(1/2, chi_{8d})^4 = X P(log X) + o(X), decide whether the error term can be improved to a power saving, and determine whether the Multiple Dirichlet Series method can recover at least the initial coefficients of P.
target_in_paper: Problems section, Problem (19): the unsmoothed fourth moment of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions in the family chi_{8d}, asking for the full degree-10 main-term polynomial, a possible power-saving error term, and whether the Multiple Dirichlet series method can recover the first coefficients.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's official formulation. It correctly identifies the right family (quadratic characters chi_{8d} with d odd squarefree), the right moment (the fourth moment at s=1/2), the existence of a degree-10 polynomial main term X P(log X), and the two follow-up issues explicitly asked in the paper: whether o(X) can be improved to a power-saving error term, and whether the Multiple Dirichlet series method can recover coefficients of P.
missing_details: The asymptotic variable should be stated explicitly: the statement is as X -> infinity.
The sum should be written explicitly as ranging over positive odd square-free d with 0 < d < X.
The character should be identified exactly as the quadratic Dirichlet character associated to the fundamental discriminant 8d.
P should be described as a one-variable polynomial evaluated at log X, of degree exactly 10.
The paper asks specifically whether the error term o(X) can be replaced by a power-saving error term; a stand-alone version should make this explicit, e.g. O(X^{1-delta}) for some delta > 0.
The Multiple Dirichlet series clause in the paper is about obtaining the first coefficients of P; your phrase 'at least the initial coefficients' is close but less faithful to the paper's wording.

A nearby note in the paper records that Shen and Stucky have already determined the first four coefficients of P; this is not part of the open problem itself, but it is relevant context if the question is meant to be fully paper-faithful.
refined_question: As X -> infinity, determine a polynomial P(x) of degree 10 such that sum_{0<d<X, d odd square-free} L(1/2, chi_{8d})^4 = X P(log X) + o(X), where chi_{8d} denotes the quadratic Dirichlet character associated to the fundamental discriminant 8d. Can the error term o(X) be sharpened to a power-saving error term O(X^{1-delta}) for some delta > 0? Can the Multiple Dirichlet series method be used to obtain the first coefficients of P?
justification: This draft targets Problem (19) in the paper almost verbatim. The exact open problem on page 9 asks for a degree-10 polynomial P satisfying the fourth-moment asymptotic for the family chi_{8d}, then separately asks about a power-saving improvement to the o(X) error term and whether the Multiple Dirichlet series method can recover the first coefficients of P. The immediately preceding Problem (18) on page 8 fixes the same family and notation for chi_{8d}, and the introduction explains that Multiple Dirichlet Series is one of the two principal methods for studying moments of L-functions. The note after Problem (19) adds the paper-faithful context that Shen and Stucky have already determined the first four coefficients, so the refined question should not broaden beyond the remaining open task.
